transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, yeah… I guess I’m here because of elevators. Which sounds kind of ridiculous when I say it, because I work around construction stuff and loud equipment and all that, and you’d think an elevator wouldn’t be the thing, you know? But when I have to get in one, I just get this fear like I’m going to be stuck or trapped in there, and I know in my head they’re not really dangerous. I do know that. I just can’t make myself feel normal about it.
Do you ever have episodes where you feel an intense fear or discomfort when you're in an elevator that reaches a peak within minutes?

Yeah, it’s pretty much right away. Like as soon as the doors start sliding shut, my chest gets tight and my hands get sweaty, and I’m just thinking, I need to get out. Even if it’s only a couple floors, which is dumb because I’ve been in worse spots at work, like tight stairwells or those little job trailers packed with people, but the elevator doors closing just… it hits fast.
Do you ever have these intense fear episodes in situations other than being in an elevator?

I don’t… I mean, not that I’ve really noticed. It’s mostly the elevator thing. Like, I can be on a job site with noise and people yelling and machines backing up, and I’m more annoyed than scared, you know? Although sometimes those sites are so chaotic, especially when somebody parks the lift in the wrong place and everyone’s blaming everyone else—but no, sorry, I’m getting off track. I don’t think I get that same intense feeling in other situations.
Do you find yourself avoiding elevators because of this fear?

Yeah… I avoid them a lot. Most days I’ll take the stairs at my apartment, and on job sites too, even if it’s a pain with boots and tools and all that. I tell myself it’s good exercise, which I guess it is, but really it’s because I don’t want to get in the elevator.

And if it’s one of those lifts or an elevator is the only way up, I’ll try to get put on something else if I can. If I absolutely have to ride it, I need somebody I trust right there with me. Like, not just some random guy from another crew who thinks it’s funny to mess around with the buttons—people do that kind of stuff on sites, you know? But yeah, I do avoid them.
Do you ever have episodes of intense fear or discomfort that are not related to being in an elevator?

Not really, no. I mean, I get stressed like anybody—work stuff, people yelling, schedules getting messed up, that kind of thing—but that’s not the same. The really intense fear feeling, where it kind of grabs me fast, that’s tied to the elevator. At least that’s the only place I’ve noticed it.
Have you ever had an episode of intense fear or discomfort that wasn't related to being in an elevator?

I don’t think so… not that I can remember. I mean, I get worked up about other stuff sometimes, like if the foreman’s rushing everybody or somebody does something dumb on site and it throws the whole day off, but that’s more aggravating than that fear feeling. The intense kind of fear, I only really notice it with elevators.
Have you ever had an episode of intense fear or discomfort that wasn't related to being in an elevator and seemed to come out of the blue, without any obvious cause?

I don’t think so, no… not out of nowhere like that. If I get really uncomfortable, there’s usually something going on, like the elevator thing.

I mean, sometimes at work everything’s loud and rushed and somebody’s yelling because a delivery’s late or whatever, and I’ll feel tense, but that’s not really coming out of the blue. That’s just a bad day on a site, you know? The fear feeling I’ve been talking about, I don’t notice that unless it’s tied to the elevator.
Have you ever had an episode where you felt an intense fear or discomfort that seemed to come out of the blue, without being in an elevator?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, if I’m upset, there’s usually a reason, like work being a mess or somebody getting on my nerves. But just sudden fear out of nowhere, without the elevator being part of it… I haven’t really had that, not that I can think of.
Have you ever had an episode where you felt an intense fear or discomfort that wasn't related to an elevator and seemed to come out of the blue?

I’m not really sure I’ve had that. Like, out of the blue? No, not that I’ve noticed.

Sometimes I get stressed if the day’s going sideways—like at work, when everybody’s waiting on somebody else and then somehow it becomes my problem—but that’s not the same thing. That’s more just being irritated or wound up. I can’t think of a time where I was just sitting there and suddenly got really scared for no reason.
Have you ever had a sudden episode of intense fear or discomfort that wasn't related to being in an elevator?

No, not really. I mean, I get worked up sometimes, sure, but there’s usually a reason—like somebody rushing me at work or plans getting messed up. That’s different. I can’t think of a time where it just hit me out of nowhere and it wasn’t about the elevator.
Have you ever had a panic attack that wasn't related to being in an elevator?

No, I don’t think so. Not like a panic attack just happening for no reason. I mean, I’ve gotten really stressed before—work can be a lot, especially when people don’t clean up after themselves and then you’re the one trying to move around all the junk—but that’s more me getting annoyed or tense. If it’s that really scared feeling, it’s been tied to the elevator thing, not just out of nowhere.
